_about: Every model file RoleMatch has fetched: where it came from, its licence, its exact hash. Files live in server/data/models/ (git-ignored) or in Ollama. Rule: free, permissive licences only, no paid licensing (docs/architecture/AI_PHASE_PLAN.md section 0). A model is used in the platform only after it passes the promotion gate; 'smoke-tested' means it loads and behaves sensibly, nothing more.

models.notes: Found the K8s sentence for 'Kubernetes administration'; missed 'presentation skills'. Similarities sit in a narrow band (0.80 to 0.86), so a threshold alone will not separate good from bad matches.

models.role: reranker (does this sentence support this requirement)
models.licence: Apache-2.0 (base model; the ONNX conversion's card names the base model and no other licence)
models.notes: Diagnosed 2026-10-23: the model card's own example scores 0.995 (logit 5.32 against the published 5.26), so the pipeline and the 8-bit file are fine. The low score was the abbreviation: 'Managed production K8s clusters' 0.004, the same sentence with 'Kubernetes' 0.58, an unrelated sentence 0.000. General models do not know our abbreviations, so text is canonicalised through the vocabulary (K8s -> Kubernetes) before the reranker sees it (src/ai/vocabulary.ts).
Degree-reading check, 5 requirements with written definitions: 3 of 5, about 0.8 s each; quotes always in the text; 'equivalent accepted' right 5 of 5.
Same check: 4 of 5, about 1.4 s each. Both models read a bare 'Bachelor's degree' as completed-required, a judgement the recruiter approves.
